text:
CAR arrives at Edmonton after a 6-3 win in Vancouver, the Canucks' eighth straight game without a win, and they're 4-1-0 in their last five. They're doing it without Taylor Hall, Mark Jankowski and Jordan Staal. With Hall out, Bradly Nadeau has taken his spot beside Logan Stankoven and Jackson Blake. EDM is also 4-1-0 over its last five, and Evan Bouchard won Tuesday's game against MIN in overtime. Jason Dickinson is out.

The numbers split the teams. Expected goals measure the quality of chances. At five on five, CAR has taken 58% of them in its games, EDM 50%. The Oilers' +14 goal difference runs ahead of their chances, with finishing doing the lifting. The model projects 3.28 goals for CAR and 2.80 for EDM. CAR takes 4.2 penalties a game, which keeps handing opponents power plays. In net, projected starters Brandon Bussi (CAR, -2.2 goals saved above expected, a measure of saves beyond what shot quality predicts) and Devon Levi (EDM, +0.8) meet. Levi has stopped .931 over his last five starts. Bussi had +1.15 over 39 games last season.

Connor McDavid (9-game point streak, 89% to record a point) and Leon Draisaitl (41% to score) lead the Oilers' watch list. For CAR, Sebastian Aho is 33% to score and 70% to get a point, while Jackson Blake sits two points from 100 career points and Nikolaj Ehlers one from 600.
